answers.question: Within how many minutes must a mine operator call MSHA after an accident that kills a miner?
answers.answer: The operator must contact MSHA within 15 minutes, once the operator knows or should know that the accident has occurred. A miner's death is an accident that triggers this requirement.

claims.text: The operator must contact MSHA immediately and within 15 minutes of knowing or having reason to know of an accident.
claims.quote: The operator shall immediately contact MSHA at once without delay and within 15 minutes at the toll-free number, 1-800-746-1553, once the operator knows or should know that an accident has occurred involving:

claims.text: A death of an individual at the mine is one of the listed accidents that triggers the notification.
claims.quote: (a) A death of an individual at the mine;

answers.question: What minimum incombustible content must the combined dust in an underground coal mine keep where no methane is present?
answers.answer: The incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust must be not less than 80 percent. The 0.4 percent increase per 0.1 percent of methane applies only where methane is present.

claims.text: The incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust must be not less than 80 percent.
claims.quote: maintained in such quantities that the incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust shall be not less than 80 percent.

claims.text: The increase applies only where methane is present in a ventilating current: 0.4 percent for each 0.1 percent of methane.
claims.quote: Where methane is present in any ventilating current, the percent of incombustible content of such combined dust shall be increased 0.4 percent for each 0.1 percent of methane.

answers.question: How long must the self-rescue device given to each underground coal miner be able to protect that person?
answers.answer: The device must be adequate to protect the person for 1 hour or longer.

claims.text: Under 30 CFR 75.1714, the self-rescue device made available to each underground miner must be adequate to protect the person for 1 hour or longer.
claims.quote: an approved self-rescue device or devices which is adequate to protect such person for 1 hour or longer.

answers.question: How often must an underground metal or nonmetal mine hold evacuation drills?
answers.answer: An underground metal or nonmetal mine must hold mine evacuation drills at least once every six months. The drills must be held for each shift, at a time other than a shift change.

claims.text: Underground evacuation drills must be held at least once every six months.
claims.quote: At least once every six months, mine evacuation drills shall be held

claims.text: Drills must be held for each shift at some time other than a shift change.
claims.quote: Be held for each shift at some time other than a shift change and involve all persons underground;

answers.question: How many hours of training must a new underground miner receive before being assigned to work duties?
answers.answer: A new underground miner must receive no less than 40 hours of training before being assigned to work duties, with approximately 8 hours given at the minesite.

claims.text: Each new underground miner must receive no less than 40 hours of training before being assigned to work duties.
claims.quote: Each new miner shall receive no less than 40 hours of training as prescribed in this section before such miner is assigned to work duties.

claims.text: Approximately 8 of those hours are given at the minesite.
claims.quote: approximately 8 hours of training shall be given at the minesite.

answers.question: What is the permissible exposure level for noise at a mine, as an 8-hour average?
answers.answer: The permissible exposure level is a TWA8 (8-hour time-weighted average) of 90 dBA, which is equivalent to a dose of 100% of that permitted by the standard.

claims.text: The permissible exposure level is a TWA8 of 90 dBA, equivalently a dose of 100% of that permitted by the standard.
claims.quote: Permissible exposure level. A TWA8 of 90 dBA or equivalently a dose of 100% of that permitted by the standard

answers.question: How high must berms or guardrails be on the banks of roadways at metal and nonmetal mines?
answers.answer: At metal and nonmetal mines, berms or guardrails must be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway. The rule is the same in the surface (56.9300) and underground (57.9300) versions.

claims.text: Berms or guardrails must be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment that usually travels the roadway (57.9300).
claims.quote: Berms or guardrails shall be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway.

claims.text: The same height requirement appears in 56.9300.
claims.quote: Berms or guardrails shall be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway.

answers.question: For how many hours must the breathable air in an approved refuge alternative sustain each person?
answers.answer: 96 hours. The breathable air must sustain each person for 96 hours. A refuge alternative that sustains persons for only 48 hours is allowed if advance arrangements are made for additional supplies.

claims.text: Within the refuge alternative, the breathable air must sustain each person for 96 hours.
claims.quote: The breathable air sustains each person for 96 hours,

claims.text: A refuge alternative may sustain persons for only 48 hours if advance arrangements are made to provide additional supplies to those not rescued within 48 hours.
claims.quote: If the refuge alternative sustains persons for only 48 hours, the ERP shall detail advanced arrangements that have been made to assure that persons who cannot be rescued within 48 hours will receive additional supplies to sustain them until rescue.
